patch.value: Release candidate acceptance hard-codes the pre-bump CLI version and blocks the daily cut

The current-main Auto Release pipeline synchronizes package.json to the date-version candidate before running coverage. The packaged runtime-compatibility acceptance test asserts a literal prior CLI version in stderr, so correct candidate behavior fails the release gate after version synchronization.

The packaged test obtains the executing CLI version rather than embedding a date version; focused and exact 100/100/100/100 coverage gates pass; exact-head PR checks and reviews pass; one v2026.8.8 tag/package is published and verified through npm, npx, and bunx; the failed run and recovery are recorded on the release-health lineage
Restore candidate-version-independent release acceptance without weakening the runtime warning contract
Daily release gates validate behavior across version synchronization instead of encoding yesterday's package metadata
The first post-merge release is blocked and no 2026.8.8 artifact exists
GitHub Actions Auto Release run 31258567364 on merged main 589b0d217

Run the release pipeline after candidate version synchronization; coverage fails in tests/unit/sdk/project-runtime-compatibility.spec.ts because stderr reports Running 2026.8.8 while the assertion expects Running 2026.8.7.
Packaged acceptance derives the executing CLI version and remains valid before and after the date-version candidate bump; the guarded release completes exactly once.
Auto Release run 31258567364 failed with one assertion after 7,061 passing tests; no tag or package was published.
